value: hourly mean detections peaked during crepuscular periods
method: passive acoustic telemetry: external coded acoustic transmitters (Innovasea V8-4H) on wild-caught palenose parrotfish, positions from a receiver array; hourly mean detections
conditions: Wild palenose parrotfish at Puako, leeward coast of the Island of Hawai'i (South Kohala). Eight palenose parrotfish tagged (of 16 parrotfish captured at night with mesh nets, the other eight being ember parrotfish) on 13 and 17 June 2012 and tracked from 12 June to 15 July 2012 (printed '6/12/2012 to 7/15/2012'; positioning system in place for 35 days). The same abstract sentence says the peak held 'to a lesser extent' for ember parrotfish (Scarus rubroviolaceus), which is not filed here. Preceding abstract sentence: home ranges and core use of both species were significantly larger during the day than at night. Abstract also says both species were mostly detected on the fore reef during the day with no reef-flat use at night, and that night data were too sparse to estimate activity spaces; the peak is read by the authors as movement between shallower daytime (foraging) and nighttime (resting) areas. The abstract opens with the background remark that parrotfishes are known to be strictly diurnal. The text read did not state how long fish were held after capture.

value: larger horizontal core areas and vertical areas of extent during crepuscular and night periods than during the day
method: passive acoustic telemetry: Vemco V13P depth-sensing transmitters implanted in wild adults, two lines of ten VR2W receivers; activity-space (core area and extent) compared among day, dawn, dusk and night periods
conditions: Wild adult redthroat emperor at the northern reef slope of Heron Island Reef, Capricorn-Bunker region, Great Barrier Reef, Australia; monitoring 22 March to 22 June 2014. Fish caught by rod and reel on barbless hooks and surgically tagged; 11 tagged, of which 5 were analysed (four dropped because their detection patterns suggested they had died); seven detected fish measured 376-464 mm fork length. Dawn 0400-0659 and dusk 1700-1959 h; day and night windows centred on midday and midnight, other hours excluded as buffers. The value is activity-space size by period, not a direct activity count. Abstract: vertical space use (core area and extent) was consistently larger during dawn, dusk and night than during the day; area of activity space and overlap among periods varied among weeks, with a pattern consistent with full moon periods. Conclusions: although earlier evidence suggested adults may shift to deeper habitat adjacent to the reef slope at night, greater space use across the shallow crest to deeper sand habitat was observed at dawn, dusk and night. Authors attribute this to increased luminosity at those periods enlarging the search area (inference).

value: all tracked fish were active during both sunrise and sunset; some individuals had prolonged activity hours to variable extents
method: passive acoustic telemetry (Vemco receivers) on wild-caught tagged fish; individual diel activity hours from detections
conditions: Wild common lionfish in their native range, sub-tropical fringing reef off Eilat, Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea; 13 Vemco receivers deployed May 2017 to February 2019. 11 fish tagged, 8 survived and their detections were analysed. Fish captured at night by SCUBA divers with hand nets. The paper's finding is large individual-level variability in activity hours; individuals often changed their patterns over time (low repeatability); depth preference also varied among individuals. The abstract also notes that nocturnal individuals from deeper waters possibly replenishing diurnally culled shallow populations. No single population-level category (diurnal or nocturnal) is stated; the value is the sentence's own statement about sunrise and sunset activity.
